starvationMultiplier.note: Multiplier on diseaseDaily under supply shortfall. Engels app.1: reduced rations for more than a few days bring "malnutrition and starvation"; magnitude is an educated guess.

winterExposure.note: Multiplier on diseaseDaily in winter outside towns. SG 1944: continental US noneffective rate peaked in December with the respiratory epidemic (40 per 1,000 per day in Jan-Feb). Magnitude educated guess; high end for 1812-type exposure.

desertHeat.note: Multiplier on diseaseDaily in desert summer. Educated guess: Engels shows water needs nearly doubling in heat and hard work (horses 5-15 gal/day by temperature) and the Gedrosian march as the campaign's worst attrition (high end).

desertionDaily.note: At morale <= 0.5. Educated guess: levies and tribal hosts melt away within weeks.

France: Carnot reported 175,000 deserters by 1800; Italian kingdom ~40,000 deserters in the Napoleonic wars. Rate per day at low morale is a composite.
American Civil War: Union ~200,000 desertions from ~2.5M men, Confederacy 103,400 from <1M over 4 years = ~0.0002/day average, concentrated in low-morale periods (x2-3).
Irish Army 1940-45: ~7,000 of 60,000 deserted (~0.00006/day at low morale, no war); belligerent armies with harsh discipline similar. Educated guess.

returnToDuty.note: SG 1944: ~1 admission per man per year with a disease noneffective stock of ~31 per 1,000 per day = ~11 days lost per case, low mortality -> most WWII cases returned (high). Pre-modern case fatality much higher (low). Mid composite.
